blocking.issue: The hot-key rule cannot hold as written. Every locally admitted request still runs GCRA, and the healthy derived ceiling is 2 x `requests` / N_published per Node, so a key sends up to N x ceiling = 2 x `requests` calls per window to its shard, and more while the count lags. At the stated 50% threshold, a key just under the threshold may therefore use 100% of a shard's about 100,000 calls per second (hypothesis). That contradicts CE-12's pass criteria (shard script CPU under 70%, no co-tenant breaker opens) and the 62.5% per-shard assumption in Cell sizing. The MUST also has no mechanism behind it. It relies on 'local-only enforcement (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1)', which is only option (c) of that question, while its owner recommends option (a) (`config.perNodeCeiling`, `config.burst`), which does not stop GCRA per admitted request. A local-only mode also departs from pack 8.8 ('each locally admitted request runs GCRA'), yet OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 does not list it among the pack 8.8 amendments.
blocking.evidence: Line 293: "Every locally admitted request still runs GCRA, so calls are at least the admitted rate, and no ceiling cuts them below the limit. A key whose `requests` per second exceeds 50% of one shard's calls, about 50,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use local-only enforcement (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1)". Line 607: "| CE-12 | Hot key at 10 times one shard's capacity, about 1,000,000 calls per second (hypothesis) | Calls at most N × ceiling per window; shard script CPU under 70% (target); no co-tenant breaker opens |". Traffic management Per-Node ceiling: "min(`requests`, max(10, ceil(2 × `requests` / N_published)))". Traffic management OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1: "(a) `config.perNodeCeiling`, `config.burst` (recommended); (b) a headroom multiplier; (c) `localOnly` mode". Worked case: `requests: 49000` per `1s` on 100 Nodes gives a ceiling of 980, so the key can send 98,000 GCRA calls per second, 98% of one shard (hypothesis).
blocking.fix: Derive the threshold from the call bound. Calls reach at most 2 x `requests` x N_serving / N_published, so a key MUST go local-only when 2 x `requests` exceeds 70% of one shard's calls: about 35,000 per second at steady state, or 25% (about 25,000 per second, hypothesis) to leave margin for count lag. Apply the same figure in the hot-key row of Cell and Cluster bottlenecks, in OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-15 and in CE-12, whose tested key limit must sit below it. State that the MUST needs option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (a `localOnly` mode), alone or alongside (a). Add that pack 8.8 amendment, with its fail-open and healthy bound of N_serving x ceiling per window (target), to OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 and to the bounds table.

blocking.issue: The Quota denial cache has no size ceiling. Its only bound is a TTL, and neither this document nor Traffic management puts it inside the shared 1,048,576-entry key table. The number of entries therefore grows with the number of distinct exhausted keys seen in 60 s, which breaks SG-7 ('Every per-Node structure has a ceiling') and leaves an unbounded-memory path. A custom `config.key`, for example one that includes `source.ip`, multiplies the number of distinct keys.
blocking.evidence: Line 69: "| Quota denial cache | 60 s per key (target) | Next Quota script | The counter is re-read |". Line 42: "| SG-7 | Every per-Node structure has a ceiling, and every accuracy bound is a tagged number | P10 |". Traffic management Quotas: "Nodes cache the denial, keyed with the limit, up to 60 s (target)". Traffic management says only rate-limit "Buckets, local-only and over-limit entries share a Node-wide 1,048,576 entries", and the Quota denial cache is not among them.
blocking.fix: Give the row an entry bound. Either place Quota denials in the shared CLOCK-evicted key table ('shares the 1,048,576-entry table (target)') or give them their own segment, for example 65,536 entries (target), with CLOCK eviction. State why eviction is safe: an evicted denial only costs one more Quota script. Add the segment to the Per-Node limits table and to the memory sum under it.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 355 (local-only row under OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 (a)) uses the healthy, floored ceiling min(`requests`, max(10, ...)). Show the worked number: 10 per `1s` on 100 Nodes admits up to 1,000 per second, 100 x the limit, for the 10 s entry lifetime (hypothesis). Readers otherwise assume the fail-open, unfloored figure.

The pass criterion 'the published count drops at most 10% (target)' in CE-7 and CE-10 holds only under OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a). Control plane and GitOps currently says 'large decreases publish at once' and counts only streams connected for 10 minutes. Mark both criteria 'under OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a)'.

State client in-flight calls count 'until its reply or a connection reset'. State which read or write deadline resets a black-holed pipelined connection (for example a rueidis connection timeout, once the research file covers it). Otherwise the size of the stuck-call leak toward the 8,192 ceiling depends on TCP keepalive.

The roughly 470 MiB sum leaves out byte bounds for the Response Cache revalidation queue (256 saved requests, each with headers of up to 256 KiB, about 64 MiB worst case), the 8,192-span queue and `/tap` buffers. Add byte caps, or say that the sum covers only the listed rows.

'First-seen budget, Plugin key-rate and Semantic Cache concurrency counters | One counter each' understates the state. Plugin key-rate is per Policy, and if '10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute' counts distinct keys it needs a set of up to 10,000 x 256 bytes per Policy. State the bound.
Line 163 tags '5,000 streams each' as (target) through the trailing tag, while Control plane and GitOps and line 585 give it as (hypothesis). Tag it (hypothesis) on line 163 as well.

Figure 3 has no branch for the local-only entry that option (a) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 would add (admit with no GCRA call). Add an 'alt local-only entry (proposed)' branch, or say in the caption that the figure shows the conforming option (c).

Persisting the Node count under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 (c)) also changes the P4 wording in Vision and positioning ('no durable state beyond ...'). Name P4 in OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 next to pack 8.11.
Make the Drain rule include the post-commit flush of up to 5 s (target): `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` MUST exceed preStop plus drain deadline plus flush.

ac_results.ac: Each of the 11 scalability_items is an H2 or H3 heading or a named pointer link
ac_results.note: The H2s cover stateless data plane, horizontal scaling, high availability and multi-region. The H3s under Distributed state catalog cover distributed rate limits, caches and sessions. Named links under Pointers cover performance budgets, benchmarking, capacity planning and zero-downtime upgrades.

ac_results.ac: Distributed state catalog has at least 10 rows with columns state, store, consistency, algorithm and failure mode, and no blank cells
ac_results.note: 11 rows, the exact columns, no blank cells. The verify script has no FAIL line.

ac_results.ac: Stateless data plane contains an inventory of every in-memory per-Node state and why losing it is safe
ac_results.note: The inventory now covers State client, cache coalescing and LRU, INFO readings, first-seen and `/tap` state. The Quota denial cache row lacks a size ceiling (L1-2), but the inventory and safety column are present.

ac_results.ac: Horizontal scaling covers the scale unit, autoscaling signals, SO_REUSEPORT, L4 load balancing and warm-up
ac_results.note: An H3 covers each. The CPU threshold is now derived from the zone count.

ac_results.ac: High availability covers Ruralz Gateway, Ruralz Control and the State Store, and Ruralz Control outage behavior is consistent with Control plane and GitOps (Last-Known-Good)
ac_results.note: Matches the 5 s wait then Last-Known-Good boot, `detached`, held Enrollment and the fencing rule. The concurrent fencing region resolves the earlier diagram defect.

ac_results.note: 'Global quota accuracy bound (target)' gives 0% over-admission in one healthy Cell, R x across Cells, plus tagged failover and layout-switch terms.

ac_results.ac: Multi-region covers topologies, regional versus global quotas, geo and data-residency routing, cross-region configuration sync and latency budgets
ac_results.note: An H3 covers each, with the divided-Quota YAML and Figure 4.
